subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What policy should OpenClaw use when active SecretRef providers fail during supervised gateway startup?
rationale: The code can be changed in several plausible ways, but retrying, degrading startup, failing closed, adding config, or delegating to external resolvers have different security and operator-recovery tradeoffs that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Adopt bounded generic startup mitigation
options.body: Add a core startup-only retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy with clear logs, focused tests, and no provider-specific 1Password assumptions.

options.title: Keep fail-fast and document operations
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed startup contract and add explicit supervisor/SecretRef guidance plus external resolver recommendations for quota-sensitive deployments.

options.title: Require external resolver ownership
options.body: Close the core policy gap only if maintainers decide Varlock-style batching/caching resolvers are the supported path and no core startup behavior should change.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded generic startup mitigation
recommendation.body: Add a core startup-only retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy with clear logs, focused tests, and no provider-specific 1Password assumptions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for the SecretRef runtime snapshot and external provider contract is in joshavant's commits.
